exposure: lipid levels (total cholesterol, triglycerides, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, free fatty acids, lipoprotein-a, apolipoprotein-a1, apolipoprotein B, LDL-C/HDL-C ratio, ApoA1/ApoB ratio)
cohort: The study included 126 pregnant women with preeclampsia and 130 healthy pregnant women in late pregnancy.
finding: Maternal BMI, neonatal weight, and specific serum levels (uric acid, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol) were identified as risk factors and valuable predictive indicators for preeclampsia.
mod_finding: No significant differences were observed between the preeclampsia and control groups in terms of mode of delivery.
birth_weight: Not specified as an inclusion criterion; neonatal weight was an outcome/factor.
gest_age: Not specified as an inclusion criterion; participants were in late pregnancy.
